integrity: For \(n\ge4\), an explicit surviving-geodesic argument proves that deleting any edge not incident with a fixed probe leaves all distances from that probe unchanged. Thus each probe monitors exactly its incident edges, reducing distance-edge monitoring exactly to vertex cover. The crown independent sets are precisely one-side subsets together with the deleted matched pairs, yielding the stated polynomial by complementation. A direct distance-recomputation verifier independently checks every subset for \(4\le n\le7\) and the exceptional case \(n=3\).
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to crown graphs \(\operatorname{Cr}_n\) with \(n\ge4\).
The boundary graph \(\operatorname{Cr}_3\cong C_6\) has distance-edge-monitoring number \(2\) and does not satisfy the incident-edge-only property.
No classification is claimed for unequal complete bipartite graphs with a matching deleted or for nonperfect matching deletion.
The finite verification through \(n=7\) is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed crown treatment may exist despite targeted searches.
title: Distance-edge-monitoring sets of crown graphs
